title: Rethinking the Role of Tool Graph Memory in Multi-Turn Tool Use
abstract: arXiv:2610.21571v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents solve complex tasks by calling external tools over multiple turns. Recent work has proposed tool graph memory, which stores past experience as tool transitions to guide subsequent selection. However, it remains unclear whether this component consistently improves agents' tool use or undermines it. We evaluate tool graph memory on nine models and two benchmarks, finding that it seldom improves significantly over baselines, and that its gains, where present, cost over twice the LLM calls. The memory's guidance is often incorrect, and random or no guidance retains most of the gain, implying that the benefit stems from extra computation rather than the memory itself. Moreover, even with the correct next tool suggested, many failures remain, such as giving up without a tool call. translated_title: 重新思考工具图记忆在多轮工具使用中的作用
translated_abstract: 大语言模型（LLM）智能体通过在多轮交互中调用外部工具来解决复杂任务。近期的研究提出了工具图记忆，它将过去的经验以工具转移的形式存储，用以指导后续的工具选择。然而，这一组件究竟是一致地改善了智能体的工具使用，还是反而削弱了它，目前仍不清楚。我们在九个模型和两个基准上对工具图记忆进行了评估，发现它很少能显著超越基线方法，而且其收益（在存在的情况下）需要付出超过两倍的LLM调用成本。这种记忆提供的指导常常是不正确的，而随机指导或不提供指导仍能保留大部分收益，这意味着收益来源于额外的计算而非记忆本身。此外，即使给出了正确的下一个工具建议，许多失败仍然存在，例如在没有调用工具的情况下放弃任务。将相同的经验改以文本洞察的形式存储，则能在几乎不增加LLM调用的情况下超越工具图记忆。这表明……
tldr: 研究发现工具图记忆对LLM智能体多轮工具使用的收益主要来自额外的计算而非记忆本身，而将经验以文本洞察形式存储可以几乎零额外成本地取得更好的效果。
en_tdlr: This study finds that the benefits of tool graph memory in multi-turn tool use stem from extra computation rather than the memory itself, and storing the same experience as textual insights outperforms it with almost no additional LLM calls.
